item.title: F5 says hackers stole undisclosed BIG-IP flaws, source code
item.description:
📝 cybersecurity company F5 disclosed that nation-state hackers breached its systems and stole undisclosed BIG-IP security vulnerabilities and source code. The company also states that it has not seen evidence that the private information has been disclosed. Despite any evidence "of undisclosed critical or remote code execution vulnerabilities," the company urges customers to prioritize installing the new BIG-IP software updates.
🔗 Read more: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/f5-says-hackers-stole-undisclosed-big-ip-flaws-source-code/

item.title: Recursive Language Models (RLMs)
item.description:
📝 Recursive Language Models We propose Recursive Language Models (RLMs), an inference strategy where language models can decompose and recursively interact with input context of unbounded length through REPL environments. Recursive Language Models (RLMs). A recursive language model call replaces a language model call.
🔗 Read more: https://alexzhang13.github.io/blog/2025/rlm/

item.title: Are hard drives getting better?
item.description:
📝 In Drive Failure Over Time: The Bathtub Curve Is Leaking, we challenged one of reliability engineering’s oldest ideas—the notion that drive failures trace a predictable U-shaped curve over time. Drives are getting better—or, more precisely, the Drive Stats dataset says that our drives are performing better in data center environments. And, this is what it looks like: The classic bathtub curve.
🔗 Read more: https://www.backblaze.com/blog/are-hard-drives-getting-better-lets-revisit-the-bathtub-curve/

item.description:
